name: Home inspector

pf.license.need: Home inspection: a state license for each inspector where the state licenses home inspectors, and a company license where the state asks for one too. Some states license nobody: then registration only. Radon testing: its own license or certificate where the state requires one. A termite (wood-destroying insect) report: only a holder of the state's pest-control license, where one is required.
pf.license.ask: Each inspector's license number and type. The company's license number, where the state's form asks for one. Each radon tester's license or certificate number, where required.
pf.license.who_holds: Each inspector holds their own license. The company holds its own where the state asks. A partner pest company holds the termite license, never this business.
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks_live: Where the state licenses inspectors: no inspection is offered until the company's and the inspector's numbers check out. An add-on that needs its own license is offered only with someone who holds it.
pf.license.insurance_bond: Errors-and-omissions or general liability insurance, or a bond, where the state's form requires it. Shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
pf.license.background_checks: Only where the state's rules require them, or as the business's own word.
pf.license.shown_to_customers: The inspector's license number on offers, confirmations and the report, where the state's rules require it.
pf.license.drone: A roof viewed by drone: only by a pilot who meets the federal rules for flying for pay. The plug-in never offers a drone view unless Sam says his pilot qualifies.
pf.license.not_this_work: Repairs of any kind, termite treatment and mold removal. They are other businesses' work, never booked under the inspector's plug-in.

pf.services.pattern: Set service: one inspection at the property, priced by the home's size, with a report ready later.

pf.visit.check_in: Most inspections start with nobody there: the inspector gets in with the lockbox code, and DONE confirms the visit. A client who meets the inspector gives the code at the door, or at the walk-through.
pf.visit.entry_codes: The lockbox code is shown only to the inspector, only on the day, and each view is logged.
pf.visit.what_is_checked: Roof (walked only if it's safe and dry), attic, structure, plumbing, electrical, heating and cooling, the water heater, windows and doors. A radon monitor is set for 48 hours. A sewer scope goes through the cleanout.
pf.visit.not_tested: Anything that can't be tested, like a furnace with the gas off, is listed as not tested. A return trip is offered for the trip fee, with the client's OK.
pf.visit.walk_through: Findings only: no repair prices and no repair offers.
pf.visit.changes_at_visit: An add-on (a sewer scope, a radon test) only if the client says yes first, priced before it's done. The fee never depends on what's found or on the sale closing.
pf.visit.proof_done: DONE from the inspector's phone, with photos. The report follows by the date promised.
pf.visit.report: Sent on a secure link by the date promised at booking. Where the state's rules set a deadline, Rosie tracks it and reminds Sam before it passes. A radon result is added when the monitor comes out.
pf.visit.report_release: Sam picks per service: the report goes out at once, or once the bill is paid. Where the state's rules forbid holding a report, it goes out at once.

pf.money.start: Inspections: a card saved at booking, charged at DONE. Report reviews at the office: a card saved for the fee, paid at the office after.
pf.money.other_ways: Nothing taken and the bill texted after; a card saved for the trip fee, charged only with the owner's yes; paid in full when booking (a re-inspection of repairs or a radon test); paid at closing through the title company, the business's own way, where Sam offers it.
pf.money.deposits: None by default. A deposit cap, if any: from the state form.
pf.money.fees: Late cancel, or no way in at the start time: the business's own trip fee (the example: $89). A return trip when a utility was off: the trip fee. Sam confirms each one; no answer, no fee.
pf.money.fee_rule: The fee never depends on what the report finds or on the sale closing. Pay at closing only where the fee is still owed if the sale falls through.
pf.money.tax: A sales tax line only where the state taxes inspections, from the state form.
pf.money.rosfield_fee: The usual $2 per confirmed booking. Whether a rule against agent referral fees reaches Rosfield's $2 is a question for counsel before launch.

pf.staff.licenses: Each inspector's own license, where the state licenses inspectors. Radon testers hold their own license or certificate where required.
pf.staff.stand_in: Another inspector with the same license and skills may stand in, with the client's OK first.
pf.staff.supervision: A trainee inspects only with a licensed inspector on the job, where the state's rules allow trainees.
pf.staff.who_oks: Sam OKs quotes over $500 and every fee. Pat, the office manager, may too; Sam's answer wins.

pf.rules.agreement: A signed pre-inspection agreement before the inspection starts, where the state's rules require it. The state's form lists any clause it voids, like a liability cap below the required insurance, so Sam can check his own.
pf.rules.report_deadline: The report reaches the client within the time the state's rules set, unless the client agrees in writing to a later date. Rosie tracks the date.
pf.rules.fee_independence: The fee can't depend on what's found or on the sale closing, where the state's rules say so.
pf.rules.referral_fees: No referral fee to or from a real estate agent, where the state's rules bar it.
pf.rules.repair_ban: No repair work at a home this business inspected, for the time the state's rules set. Sam can keep it as his own rule anywhere.
pf.rules.license_shown: The license number on offers, confirmations and the report, where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.records: 7 years, or longer where the state's rules ask: the agreement, the report and the photos.

matter_most: The sale falls through: an ordinary cancel, judged only by the notice given.
Access isn't set up by 5pm the day before: Sam is asked to call the agent, and the client is told. The booking stays.
The lockbox code doesn't work: the inspector texts it, the client and the access person get a link for a new code, and the walk-through moves.
A utility is off: those items are listed as not tested, and a return trip is offered for the trip fee.
The report runs late: the client hears the new date before the old one passes.
The client asks the business to fix what it found: Rosie says this business doesn't do repairs at a home it inspected.
A moved inspection carries the signed agreement and the access link to the new date.
A radon test's closed-house time moves with the inspection.
pf.edges.rest: All other edge cases are handled the generic way.

What the cleaner lacks is added: the signed pre-inspection agreement before booking (B4-57 on every inspection), access set up by the buyer's agent (own steps B6-x01, B7-x01 to B7-x03), the walk-through at a set time inside the visit, and the report that comes later (B10-25 group, words).
Flow B is the usual side: Lee Home Inspections (home inspection, plus radon testing as its second kind of work, with its own license or certificate where a state requires one). Flow A is the less usual side: Lee Inspection Center, Sam's office, where a client goes over an inspection report with an inspector (a $35 report review), at the office, by video or at the house ($75: the both-places service).
Names: Jordan and Casey become inspectors Ethan and Luis (he, as the master's pronouns); Riley and Avery become Grace and Priya, inspectors at the center (Avery's 'her' fits Priya). The master's partner Jamie is Taylor (Jamie is a cleaner pilot name). The house Alex is buying: 214 Hilltop Dr. Alex's agent: Lisa Romero. Kim's empty house: 9 Birch Ct. Offices: 310 Market St and 250 Center St.
Prices are the example business's own, not facts about inspection prices. The main inspection is $425 (a house up to 2,000 sq ft), not the master's $179: a $179 home inspection would read wrong. The rename '$179' to '$425' is safe: the master's only sums with $179 were the parts line (B9-23, off), a plan's price change (off) and the price raise (S11-54, its own sentence, now $450). Every other master number is kept: the $89 trip fee (late cancel, no way in, or a return trip), $640 for a 4-unit building quoted from the listing's photos (over Sam's $500, so Sam OKs it), $150 re-inspection of repairs (the paid-in-full example), $199 sewer scope ($249 with Sam), $160 thermal scan (the extra at the visit). Center: $35 review, $40 repair list help, $20 permit record check, $55 second opinion, $140 new build plan review, $75 at the house, $20 fee.
Inspections start at a set time (8:30am, 1:00pm): B4-83 takes '2 A set start time' (B4-84 words, with each money path's message); the master's arrival windows are renamed to set starts ('arriving 8–10am' to 'starting 8:30am' and the like) so every confirmation, reminder and move reads the same.
Money, flow B: main list|card|card (a card saved, charged at DONE), as the old flowchart. Also used: list|none|bill (nothing taken; the bill after, and the report goes out once it's paid, Sam's setting), list|hold|card (the $89 trip fee held the day before: the old flowchart's $100 deposit for far-out visits is outdated, the master's day-before hold replaces it), list|full|none (a re-inspection paid when booking), photos|card|card (a 4-unit building quoted first), list|card|own (pay at closing: Sam bills the title company his own way, the saved card covers it if the sale falls through, where the rules let the fee be owed then). Never priced at the visit (the fee can't depend on what's found), and no deposit.
Money, flow A: main list|card|counter (a card saved for the $20 fee, paid at the office), plus list|none|counter, list|full|none (a second opinion review paid when booking) and list|card|card (Saturday mornings, when Grace works alone with no front desk: the master's own reason). Video reviews also go on the saved card at DONE (S1-42).
The agreement: Sam's own pre-inspection agreement, uploaded at sign-up, set to carry the business's signature, so B4-58 signs it for the business at once (its words; the master's 24-hour wait stays for owners who sign each one). The time stays saved while Alex reads it. Rosie never writes or edits the agreement. Raised as a gap (a business's standard agreement signed for it once).
Access: the buyer doesn't control the house. After the confirmation, Alex gets a link to forward to the agent (B6-x01): Rosie never texts someone who hasn't said yes. The agent types the lockbox code (shown only to the inspector, on the day), utilities and pets, and may add a mobile with their own yes. Due 5pm the day before; B7-x01 checks it, and B7-x03 asks Sam to call the agent (the booking stays). Raised as the gap 'Access set up by someone else'.
Check-in: most inspections start with nobody there. Ethan lets himself in with the lockbox at 8:30am; Alex gives the code at the 11:30am walk-through (B8-03, B8-04 words, with t 11:30am), and B8-45 bridges back to 8:30am. No code at all: DONE confirms the visit (B8-08). 'Nobody home' (B8-10 to B8-12) is no lockbox and nobody to let him in; 'The lockbox code fails' (B8-70, B8-52, B8-53) is Kim's empty house. B8-69 and B8-70 keep 'Nobody needs to be home' only.
The walk-through (B8-39) gives findings only: no repair prices, no repair offers. 'A bigger job, over $500' is off: an inspector never quotes repairs at a home it inspects. Alex asking the business to fix the roof gets the plug-in's rule (B10-16 words); the time-limited repair ban is the state's rule where it has one, or Sam's own. Raised as the gap 'Conflict block from earlier work'.
The report: the master's 'A report is ready later' branch (B10-25, B10-19, B10-26, B10-30) carries it, with words: ready by the promised date (Fri), a deadline the state sets tracked (the master's S13-14), a later date only with the client's written OK where the rules require it, a radon result added later. On the bill path the report waits until it's paid (more lines on B9-06, B9-11, B10-25), raised as the gap 'Results released once paid'.
Kept words: 'sewer' (the sewer scope, a real inspection add-on). The leftover-word check passes without keeping plumbing or electrical: the inspector's checks are worded as 'the home's systems' in steps, and the plug-in lists them.
Plug-in splits: kept whole (splitsKept) where it's state by state: S1-60 and S2-28 (a state licenses home inspectors and each inspector, or nobody), S1-63 (the center's reviewers, where a state licenses them), A7-61 (plan reviews are Grace's alone, report reviews anyone's), A8-02 (another firm's report must be sent first). Every other split is decided with offs: no classes, spaces, sent-now work, damage hold, plan, delivery, outside check, item to the shop or permit inspection; a person's time at the center; set starts at the property; the owner never asked (B4-78); the agreement always needed (B4-57).
Off as never used: the plans (repeat visits, plan terms, plan charges), warranty or insurance paying, stock and parts, weather stops (an inspection goes ahead in rain; a wet roof is viewed from below), estimate visits and first steps that change the job, host visit days, landlord paying, stage bills, aftercare, proposals for more work, warranty claims (an inspection carries no repair warranty: a missed item is a complaint, B10-13).
No single state: every rule from the old flowchart that named a state (the signed agreement, the fee that can't depend on the sale, agent referral fees, the 12-month repair ban, the 2-day report) is a generic switch in pf.rules, 'where the state's rules require it'. 'Free to cancel until 7am on the visit day' is the master's suggested booking rule (Sam can set 24 hours before, as the old flowchart did).
For counsel before launch: where a state bars referral fees to agents, whether Rosfield's $2 counts (pf.money). Drones: the plug-in never offers a drone view unless Sam says his pilot meets the federal rules (pf.license).
Review (Oct 22): the walk-through check-in (B8-04) has no clock of its own and reads 'Skip ahead', and B8-45 reads 'Back to the start, 8:30am', so no time runs backward; Lisa's access set-up (B7-x02) now comes before the reminder; the re-inspection (paid in full) runs about 1 hour, with its walk-through about 9:15am and DONE at 9:30am. Pay at closing (list|card|own) is kept: it's a real way inspections are paid, and the fee stays owed if the sale falls through (the saved card covers it). Flow A also lists list|hold|counter: the center holds the $40 fee of the 2½-hour new build plan review (its own sign-up says so).
